nytimes_articles.abstract:
Hong Kong claimed its first Olympic medal in any sport when Lai Shan Lee clinched the women's windsurfing gold in Savannah, Ga., with one race still to sail. Lee, 25, was a medal favorite in the Mistral competition, but she faced a  stiff challenge from the 1992 gold medalist, Barbara Kendall of New Zealand. Her confidence helped. "I had a little bit better boat speed and I think better physical fitness than the others," Lee said. Her triumph made her a hero at home, as this is the last Olympics for Hong Kong before it reverts to China. 

      Mateusz Kusznierewicz of Poland also made history, winning his nation's first medal in yachting competition by clinching first in the Finn racing.   BLAIRE LARGAY

nytimes_articles.abstract:
The explosion early Saturday morning in Centennial Olympic Park did more than cast a shadow on the largest gathering of nations and athletes in history. It exposed the truth about what has been called the biggest mobilization of law enforcement and crime-fighting technology in American history. A lowly pipe bomb -- relative of the Molotov cocktail in its crude simplicity -- destroyed the confidence that there is anything anymore called security. 

     In so many proclamations over the past few months, Atlanta Olympics officials have assured the world that their security system was the best ever. Billy Payne, the irrepressible head of the Atlantic Olympic committee, went so far as  to promise that the city would be "the safest place on this wonderful planet" during the Games.

pages.title: Communications Decency Act
pages.description: 1996 federal law attempting to regulate Internet pornography
pages.abstract: The Communications Decency Act of 1996 (CDA) was the United States Congress's first legislative attempt to regulate obscene and indecent material on the Internet. In the 1997 landmark case Reno v. ACLU, the United States Supreme Court unanimously overturned most of the statute due to its restrictions on freedom of speech under the First Amendment to the U.S. Constitution. One non-speech provision of the statute, which exempted the operators of Internet services from liability for their users' actions, survived the Supreme Court's action and was severed from the statute. That provision is now known as Section 230 and remains in effect.

pages.title: Federal judiciary of the United States
pages.abstract: The federal judiciary of the United States is one of the three branches of the U.S. federal government organized under the U.S. Constitution and laws of the federal government. The U.S. federal judiciary does not include any state court, which are completely independent from the federal government. The U.S. federal judiciary consists primarily of the U.S. Supreme Court, the U.S. courts of appeals, and the U.S. district courts. It also includes a variety of other lesser federal tribunals.

When Salad Dressing Moonlights as Sauce
nytimes_articles.abstract:
SOME culinary practices are most often pursued in private. One such habit, indulged in by many a fan of haute cuisine when no one else is watching, is pouring bottled salad dressings on food. Italian dressing, for example, often finds its way onto grilled steak, while blue cheese dressing frequently tops potatoes or green beans. 

     This sub rosa practice persists because, despite its lack of elegance, it has two stellar virtues to recommend it: it is drop-dead easy, and it tastes good. So, in these hot days of the salad season, when we want cooking kept to a minimum, why not bring this culinary habit out of the closet and shine it up a bit?

But luckily for the mid-coast diner, Michael Gagne  has created a culinary oasis for summer people and local residents. Last March,  he opened the Robinhood Free Meetinghouse restaurant, outside Bath. 

     Mr. Gagne made his culinary reputation during an eight-year tenure as chef at the nearby Osprey restaurant. At the helm of his own restaurant -- in a restored 1855 Greek Revival-style meetinghouse -- he offers an ambitious nightly menu of  31 appetizers (which include 3 soups, 11 salads and 6 fettuccine dishes), 34 entrees and 12 desserts.
